library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ahn_2020_PF06648671"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ahn_2020_PF06648671"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.1570> (open access, PMC6977340)

PF-06648671 is an oral, brain-penetrant gamma-secretase modulator (GSM). It
shifts gamma-secretase processing of the amyloid precursor protein away from
the longer, more aggregation-prone amyloid-beta (Abeta) peptides Abeta42 and
Abeta40 toward the shorter Abeta38 and Abeta37, leaving total Abeta unchanged.
Ahn 2020 fit one PK/PD model to plasma PF-06648671 and the four CSF Abeta
species from three phase I studies in healthy volunteers.

# Population

The analysis pooled 120 healthy volunteers from three Pfizer phase I studies
(Ahn 2020 Table 1 and Results, "Study populations"):

* **B7991001** (single ascending dose, Belgium): 18 white men, 22-55 years,
  52.8-104.0 kg; single oral doses of 2, 4, 12, 40, 120 (fasted and fed), 240
  and 360 mg, or placebo, in a crossover design. PK only.
* **B7991003** (single dose, United States): 22 subjects (21 men; 11 white,
  8 black, 1 Asian, 2 other), 21-55 years, 56.0-99.6 kg; 150 mg (n = 3),
  300 mg (n = 11) or placebo (n = 8), with serial CSF sampling through an
  indwelling lumbar catheter 2 h before and 0-36 h after the dose.
* **B7991002** (14-day multiple ascending dose, Belgium): part 1, 70 men aged
  18-55 years (52.4-107.2 kg) on 4, 12, 40, 100, 200 or 360 mg once daily or
  placebo; part 2, 10 elderly subjects aged 65-75 years (4 women) on 200 mg
  once daily or placebo. A single lumbar puncture was performed 72 h before
  the first dose and 24 h after the day-14 dose (day-14 pre-dose for the
  40 mg cohort).

The PD model was fitted to the CSF Abeta data of B7991003 and B7991002 (Figure
S2). The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Ahn_2020_PF06648671")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment PK, first-order absorption, linear elimination | n/a | Methods, "PK/PD modeling"; Table S4 |
| `lka` | log(1.49 1/h) | Table S4 |
| `lcl` | log(3.56 L/h) | Table S4 (CL/F) |
| `lvc` | log(46.3 L) | Table S4 (Vc/F) |
| `lq` | log(9.17 L/h) | Table S4 (Q/F) |
| `lvp` | log(32.8 L) | Table S4 (Vp/F) |
| `etalka` | 0.189 | Table S4, IIV (variance) on ka |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` block | 0.180, 0.0679, 0.0671 | Table S4, IIV on CL/F, covariance CL-Vc, IIV on Vc/F |
| `etalvp` | 0.0867 | Table S4, IIV on Vp/F |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.164, 0.462 ng/mL | Table S4, proportional CV 16.4%, additive SD |

| Stimulatory sigmoid IDR, `d/dt(abeta38_csf)`, `d/dt(abeta37_csf)` | n/a | Eq. (3); Figure 3 |
| `kin = kout * baseline` | n/a | Methods, text below Eq. (3) |
| `lrbase_abeta42/40/38/37` | log(1001, 7584, 2404, 702 pg/mL) | Table 2, Baseline |
| `lkout_abeta42/40/38/37` | log(0.121, 0.0835, 0.144, 0.0964 1/h) | Table 2, kout |

| `lic50_abeta42/40` | log(421, 1228 ng/mL) | Table 2, IC50 |

# Placebo drift in the serial-sampling study (Figure 1)

In B7991003 all four Abeta species rose steadily in the placebo arm over the
36 h of catheter sampling. The model adds the drift `(Pmax + eta) * time^Kp`
to each observed species only when `STUDY_B7991003 = 1`. The typical-value
profiles below reproduce the layout of Figure 1 b-e for placebo, 150 mg and
300 mg. The drug arms dip below baseline and then drift back upward with the
placebo trend, as the paper's mean profiles do.

```{r fig1-sim}
mod <- readModelDb("Ahn_2020_PF06648671")
# The four PD residual SDs are thetas (fixed at zero), not sigmas, so remove
# only the between-subject random effects for typical-value runs.
mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega")

# rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega; for these
# typical-value runs that is intended, so only that warning is muffled.
solve_tv <- function(events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tv, events = events, keep = "dose"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

grid_sd <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36)
make_typical <- function(id, dose, study_b7991003, times, ii = 0, addl = 0) {
  dose_row <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    ii = ii, addl = addl, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
    ii = 0, addl = 0L, dvid = 1L
  )
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_row, obs_rows)
  out$STUDY_B7991003 <- study_b7991003
  out$dose <- dose
  out
}

ev_fig1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_typical(1L, 0, 1, grid_sd),
  make_typical(2L, 150, 1, grid_sd),
  make_typical(3L, 300, 1, grid_sd)
)
sim_fig1 <- solve_tv(ev_fig1) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(arm = factor(ifelse(dose == 0, "Placebo", paste(dose, "mg")),
    levels = c("Placebo", "150 mg", "300 mg")
  ))
```

```{r fig1-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
sim_fig1 |>
  select(time, arm, abeta42, abeta40, abeta38, abeta37) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("abeta"), names_to = "species", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(species = factor(species,
    levels = c("abeta42", "abeta40", "abeta38", "abeta37"),
    labels = c("Abeta42", "Abeta40", "Abeta38", "Abeta37")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, linetype = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 36, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "CSF concentration (pg/mL)", linetype = NULL,
    title = "Typical CSF Abeta profiles in the serial-sampling study",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 1 b-e of Ahn 2020 (typical value, placebo drift on)."
  )
```

Over 36 h the paper's placebo-arm means (Figure 1) rise by roughly 600-700,
3,000, 1,000 and 300 pg/mL for Abeta42, Abeta40, Abeta38 and Abeta37. The
fixed Table S3 drift gives the increments below. They agree with the figure
on the paper's pg/mL scale, which confirms that Pmax is additive in pg/mL
with time in hours.

```{r fig1-placebo}
plac_36 <- sim_fig1 |>
  filter(arm == "Placebo", time %in% c(0, 36)) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  summarise(across(c(abeta42, abeta40, abeta38, abeta37), ~ diff(.x)))
knitr::kable(round(plac_36), caption = "Typical placebo drift between 0 and 36 h (pg/mL).")

# The drift is a closed form of the fixed Table S3 values; the solve must
# reproduce it exactly (same parameters on both sides).
stopifnot(
  abs(plac_36$abeta42 - 87.4 * 36^0.517) < 1e-6 * 1000,
  abs(plac_36$abeta40 - 176 * 36^0.799) < 1e-6 * 1000,
  abs(plac_36$abeta38 - 70.7 * 36^0.707) < 1e-6 * 1000,
  abs(plac_36$abeta37 - 35.0 * 36^0.598) < 1e-6 * 1000
)
```

The placebo-adjusted change at the PD Tmax is the drug effect on the
turnover states. The paper's Bayesian analysis of the observed data gives
-33%/-39% (Abeta42), -16%/-22% (Abeta40), +30%/+46% (Abeta38) and
+139%/+294% (Abeta37) at 150/300 mg (Table S2). The typical model
predictions are below. They are larger than the observed single-dose
changes for Abeta42 and Abeta40 (about -47%/-56% and -27%/-37%), close for
Abeta38, and in the right range for Abeta37. The paper notes that the
B7991003 data were highly variable and gave no clear exposure-response. The
drug-effect parameters were determined mainly by the steady-state data of
B7991002 (next sections), which the model follows closely.

```{r fig1-tmax}
sim_fig1 |>
  filter(arm != "Placebo") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    `Abeta42 (%)` = 100 * (min(abeta42_csf) / 1001 - 1),
    `Abeta40 (%)` = 100 * (min(abeta40_csf) / 7584 - 1),
    `Abeta38 (%)` = 100 * (max(abeta38_csf) / 2404 - 1),
    `Abeta37 (%)` = 100 * (max(abeta37_csf) / 702 - 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Dose = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical maximum change from baseline within 36 h of a single dose (drug effect only).")
```

# Virtual cohorts for PK

Original observed data are not available. The PK cohorts below use the PK
between-subject variability of Table S4, with 100 subjects per arm. The model
has no covariates on PK, so no demographic sampling is needed.

```{r cohorts}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200101)

sd_doses <- c(40, 120, 240, 150, 300)
sd_study <- c("B7991001", "B7991001", "B7991001", "B7991003", "B7991003")
grid_pk_sd <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)

make_cohort_sd <- function(n, dose, study, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = grid_pk_sd)
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$cmt <- "central"
  obs_rows$dvid <- 1L
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$STUDY_B7991003 <- as.integer(study == "B7991003")
  out$treatment <- paste0(study, " ", dose, " mg SD")
  dplyr::arrange(out, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(sd_doses), function(i) {
  make_cohort_sd(100L, sd_doses[i], sd_study[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * 100L)
}))

md_doses <- c(40, 100, 200, 360)
grid_pk_md <- 312 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24)
make_cohort_md <- function(n, dose, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    ii = 24, addl = 13L, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = grid_pk_md)
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$cmt <- "central"
  obs_rows$ii <- 0
  obs_rows$addl <- 0L
  obs_rows$dvid <- 1L
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$STUDY_B7991003 <- 0L
  out$treatment <- paste0("B7991002 ", dose, " mg QD day 14")
  dplyr::arrange(out, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_md <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(md_doses), function(i) {
  make_cohort_md(100L, md_doses[i], id_offset = 1000L + (i - 1L) * 100L)
}))
```

```{r simulate}
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sd, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()
sim_md <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_md, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
nca_one <- function(sim, events, start, end, params) {
  conc <- sim |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
  dose <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1) |>
    select(id, time, amt, treatment)
  if (start == 0) {
    # Pre-dose plasma concentration of an oral single dose is zero.
    conc <- bind_rows(conc, conc |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
      distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
      arrange(id, treatment, time)
  }
  intervals <- data.frame(start = start, end = end)
  for (p in params) intervals[[p]] <- TRUE
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
  as.data.frame(res)
}

nca_sd <- nca_one(sim_sd, ev_sd, 0, Inf, c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"))
nca_md <- nca_one(sim_md, ev_md, 312, 336, c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "cmin"))
nca_all <- bind_rows(nca_sd, nca_md) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table S2 reports geometric means (Tmax: median; t1/2: arithmetic mean). For
the day-14 rows `auclast` over 312-336 h is AUCtau and `cmin` is Ctrough.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~auclast, ~cmin,
  "B7991001 40 mg SD", 814.4, 1.00, 9657, 13.94, NA, NA,
  "B7991001 120 mg SD", 2429, 1.00, 41470, 19.05, NA, NA,
  "B7991001 240 mg SD", 3752, 1.00, 79200, 22.43, NA, NA,
  "B7991003 150 mg SD", 2482, 1.02, 36570, 12.83, NA, NA,
  "B7991003 300 mg SD", 3578, 1.03, 57390, 13.34, NA, NA,
  "B7991002 40 mg QD day 14", 991.0, 1.50, NA, NA, 11530, 234.3,
  "B7991002 100 mg QD day 14", 2168, 1.50, NA, NA, 25050, 595.6,
  "B7991002 200 mg QD day 14", 4595, 1.50, NA, NA, 64940, 1945,
  "B7991002 360 mg QD day 14", 5143, 1.50, NA, NA, 71530, 2072
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_all,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(
    cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h",
    auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median of 100 virtual subjects per arm) vs. Table S2. * differs from the reference by >20%."
)
```

```{r nca-check}
auc_sim <- nca_all |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
auc_ref <- published |>
  select(treatment, aucinf.obs, auclast) |>
  pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref") |>
  filter(!is.na(ref))
auc_cmp <- inner_join(auc_sim, auc_ref, by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
# A mis-transcribed CL/F, dose or the mg -> ng/mL factor moves every AUC by
# tens of percent; the centre of the per-arm differences stays well inside
# 20% (the B7991003 and the 360 mg arms sit at the two ends, see below).
stopifnot(abs(median(auc_cmp$pct)) < 20)
```

Most AUC and Cmax values agree within 20%. The exceptions are spread across
studies rather than following a model trend. The population model has one
apparent clearance (3.56 L/h) for all three studies. The NCA CL/F in Table S2
runs from 2.3-4.1 L/h in B7991001, 2.3-5.0 L/h in day-14 B7991002 and
4.1-5.2 L/h in B7991003. B7991003 subjects therefore had lower exposure than
the pooled model predicts. In the day-14 360 mg arm (CL/F 5.0 L/h), exposure
was barely higher than in the 200 mg arm; a linear model cannot reproduce
that. The simulated Tmax of 1.5 h is a sampling-grid value: the typical peak
falls between the 1 and 1.5 h samples. NCA half-lives (12.8-23 h) come from
72-96 h sampling windows and bracket the model's terminal half-life of about
16.5 h.

# Day-14 CSF Abeta changes (B7991002, Figure 4)

CSF was sampled once, 24 h after the day-14 dose (day-14 pre-dose for 40 mg),
when the drug is near steady-state trough. The paper's Figure 4 VPC cannot be
reproduced in full, because the PD between-subject variances are not
published. The spread below comes from PK variability only. The table compares the
median simulated change from baseline with the placebo-adjusted changes in
Table S2.

```{r fig4}
pd_md <- sim_md |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub("B7991002 ([0-9]+) mg.*", "\\1", treatment))) |>
  filter((dose == 40 & time == 312) | (dose != 40 & time == 336)) |>
  transmute(
    dose,
    Abeta42 = 100 * (abeta42 / 1001 - 1),
    Abeta40 = 100 * (abeta40 / 7584 - 1),
    Abeta38 = 100 * (abeta38 / 2404 - 1),
    Abeta37 = 100 * (abeta37 / 702 - 1)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-dose, names_to = "species", values_to = "pct")

pd_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~Abeta42, ~Abeta40, ~Abeta38, ~Abeta37,
  40, -15.84, -5.89, 11.15, 88.08,
  100, -43.67, -26.83, 8.55, 150.28,
  200, -58.82, -42.35, 46.48, 331.09,
  360, -64.77, -49.86, 44.65, 371.95
) |>
  pivot_longer(-dose, names_to = "species", values_to = "observed")

pd_tab <- pd_md |>
  group_by(dose, species) |>
  summarise(simulated = median(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(pd_obs, by = c("dose", "species")) |>
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = c("Abeta42", "Abeta40", "Abeta38", "Abeta37"))) |>
  arrange(species, dose)

pd_tab |>
  rename(
    `Dose (mg QD)` = dose, Species = species,
    `Simulated median (%)` = simulated, `Table S2 placebo-adjusted (%)` = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Change from baseline in CSF Abeta on day 14 of B7991002.")
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
pd_md |>
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = c("Abeta42", "Abeta40", "Abeta38", "Abeta37"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(dose), pct)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = pd_obs |> mutate(species = factor(species, levels = c("Abeta42", "Abeta40", "Abeta38", "Abeta37"))),
    aes(factor(dose), observed), colour = "red", shape = 4, size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "PF-06648671 dose (mg QD)", y = "Change from baseline (%)",
    title = "Day-14 CSF Abeta change by dose",
    caption = "Boxes: simulation with PK variability only. Crosses: Table S2 placebo-adjusted means. Compare Figure 4 of Ahn 2020."
  )
```

```{r fig4-check}
# Abeta42 and Abeta40 at 100-360 mg carry the dose-response the model was
# built on; the simulated medians track the reported placebo-adjusted
# changes there (realised gap <= 6 points; the median of 100 subjects moves
# about 1 point between cohorts). The 40 mg arm is discussed below.
dev <- pd_tab |>
  filter(species %in% c("Abeta42", "Abeta40"), dose >= 100) |>
  mutate(d = simulated - observed)
stopifnot(max(abs(dev$d)) < 10)
```

At 100-360 mg, the simulated Abeta42 and Abeta40 medians fall within 6
percentage points of the reported changes. At 40 mg the model predicts
roughly twice the reported reductions (-33% vs -16% for Abeta42). Abeta37
follows the reported dose-response: the model is 11 points below it at
40 mg and 40-75 points above it at 100-360 mg. Abeta38 does not follow it: the observed change is step-like (+9% at 100 mg, then +46% at 200 mg and
360 mg). The paper notes that the Abeta38 parameters are poorly determined
(EC50 RSE 142%, gamma RSE 97%) and leaves Abeta38 out of its steady-state
predictions for that reason.

# Steady-state dose-response (Figure 5)

Figure 5 shows the predicted average steady-state effect against the
once-daily dose. Below, each species is averaged over the dosing interval of
day 30 for a typical subject.

```{r fig5}
doses_f5 <- seq(0, 500, by = 25)
ev_f5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_f5), function(i) {
  make_typical(i, doses_f5[i], 0, seq(696, 720, by = 0.25), ii = 24, addl = 29L)
}))
ss <- solve_tv(ev_f5) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time >= 696) |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(across(c(abeta42, abeta40, abeta38, abeta37), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    pct42 = 100 * (abeta42 / 1001 - 1),
    pct40 = 100 * (abeta40 / 7584 - 1),
    pct37 = 100 * (abeta37 / 702 - 1),
    r4240 = abeta42 / abeta40,
    r4238 = abeta42 / abeta38,
    r4237 = abeta42 / abeta37
  )
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ss |>
  select(dose,
    `(a) Abeta42 % change` = pct42, `(b) Abeta40 % change` = pct40,
    `(c) Abeta37 % change` = pct37, `(d) Abeta42:Abeta40` = r4240,
    `(e) Abeta42:Abeta38` = r4238, `(f) Abeta42:Abeta37` = r4237
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-dose) |>
  ggplot(aes(dose, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "PF-06648671 dose (mg QD)", y = NULL,
    title = "Typical average steady-state effects",
    caption = "Replicates the median lines of Figure 5 of Ahn 2020."
  )
```

The paper gives several numbers from this analysis in the Results text, and
the maintainers read the 500 mg end of the median lines in Figure 5 by eye.
The typical model reproduces each of them:

```{r fig5-check}
at <- function(d) ss[ss$dose == d, ]
f5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Paper, ~Model,
  "Abeta42 % change at 75 mg", -50, at(75)$pct42,
  "Abeta40 % change at 250 mg", -50, at(250)$pct40,
  "Abeta42 % change at 500 mg (Figure 5a, read by eye)", -68, at(500)$pct42,
  "Abeta40 % change at 500 mg (Figure 5b, read by eye)", -57, at(500)$pct40,
  "Abeta37 % change at 500 mg (Figure 5c, read by eye)", 480, at(500)$pct37,
  "Abeta42:Abeta40 at 0 mg", 0.13, at(0)$r4240,
  "Abeta42:Abeta38 at 0 mg", 0.42, at(0)$r4238,
  "Abeta42:Abeta37 at 0 mg", 1.42, at(0)$r4237,
  "Abeta42:Abeta40 at 200 mg", 0.09, at(200)$r4240,
  "Abeta42:Abeta38 at 200 mg", 0.10, at(200)$r4238,
  "Abeta42:Abeta37 at 200 mg", 0.11, at(200)$r4237,
  "Abeta42:Abeta40 % change at 200 mg", -30, 100 * (at(200)$r4240 / at(0)$r4240 - 1)
)
knitr::kable(f5, digits = 3, caption = "Results-text values (Ahn 2020) vs. typical model.")

# Deterministic typical-value solves of the published parameters; the
# tolerances are the rounding of the printed values.
stopifnot(
  abs(at(75)$pct42 - (-50)) < 3,
  abs(at(250)$pct40 - (-50)) < 3,
  abs(at(500)$pct42 - (-68)) < 5,
  abs(at(500)$pct40 - (-57)) < 5,
  abs(at(500)$pct37 - 480) < 40,
  abs(at(0)$r4240 - 0.13) < 0.005,
  abs(at(0)$r4238 - 0.42) < 0.005,
  abs(at(0)$r4237 - 1.42) < 0.01,
  abs(at(200)$r4240 - 0.09) < 0.01,
  abs(at(200)$r4238 - 0.10) < 0.01,
  abs(at(200)$r4237 - 0.11) < 0.01,
  abs(100 * (at(200)$r4240 / at(0)$r4240 - 1) - (-30)) < 3
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **PD between-subject variability is not published.** Eq. (1) has an
  additive eta on the placebo magnitude Pmax, and the Discussion says the
  joint model accounts for correlated baselines and responses between
  species, but no PD variance or covariance appears in the paper or its
  supplement. The four `etapmax_*` etas are included at a fixed variance of
  zero; no other PD etas are encoded. CSF Abeta simulations therefore vary
  only through PK variability.
- **PD residual error is not published.** Each CSF endpoint carries a
  proportional residual SD fixed at zero, so simulated CSF values are model
  predictions without measurement noise.
- **Placebo drift units and time origin.** Table S3 gives no units for Pmax.
  Pmax is taken as pg/mL per h^Kp, added to the predicted concentration, with
  time in hours after the dose. This follows the Methods ("the sum of
  baseline, placebo ... and treatment effects") and matches the placebo
  increments in Figure 1. Negative times (the 2-h pre-dose sample) are given
  zero drift.
- **Placebo study indicator.** The drift applies only to the serial-CSF data
  of B7991003. It is switched on by the study indicator `STUDY_B7991003`.
  Set it to 0 for single-lumbar-puncture designs such as B7991002.
- **Food effect and elderly subjects.** Table S4 has no covariates. The food
  effect in B7991001 (Tmax delayed by 3 h, Cmax -24%, AUC +23%) and the
  roughly 20% lower day-14 exposure in elderly subjects are not part of the
  model.
- **CSF drug concentration** was not used in the model. Tubing adsorption in
  B7991003 lowered the measured CSF concentrations. Plasma concentration
  drives all four species directly.
- No erratum or correction notice for the article was found (checked
  2026-11-26).
